{{Short description|Filipina mathematician}}
'''Mari-Jo P. Ruiz''' (1943–2022) was a Filipina mathematician and professor of mathematics at [[Ateneo de Manila University]].{{r|obit}}
Ruiz specialized in [[graph theory]] and [[operations research]].{{r|profile|lux}}

==Education and career==
Ruiz grew up in Manila, and was educated at [[College of the Holy Spirit Manila]]. She graduated from [[Marymount Manhattan College]] in [[New York City]] in 1963, and soon afterward completed a master's degree at [[New York University]]. She joined the  Ateneo de Manila faculty in 1965,{{r|lux}} eight years before the school began accepting women as students.{{r|coed}}
She chose academia over a competing job offer from industry because at the time it paid slightly better.{{r|lux}} She acquired the nickname "Mustang Mary" at this time, because of the [[Ford Mustang]] that she drove.{{r|response}}

Ruiz completed her PhD at Ateneo in 1981.{{r|profile}} 
At Ateneo, she served as chair of mathematics, chair of management engineering, dean of arts and sciences, and trustee. She retired to become a professor emeritus in 2009.{{r|lux}} She died on 29 December 2022 at the age of 79.{{r|obit|legacy}} 

==Book==
With [[Jin Akiyama]], she was the author of the book ''A Day’s Adventure in Math Wonderland'' (World Scientific, 2008; translated into 7 other languages).{{r|bauer}}

==Recognition==
The College of the Holy Spirit Alumnae Foundation gave Ruiz their Distinguished Alumna in Education Award in 2001.{{r|profile}}
In 2014, Ateneo gave Ruiz their Lux-in-Domino Award.{{r|lux}}
